question: The ionization energy of hydrogen is $13.6 \text{ eV}$. How does this value relate to the Lyman series of the hydrogen spectrum?

options.A: It corresponds to the energy of the longest wavelength line in the Lyman series ($n=2 \to 1$).
options.B: It corresponds to the series limit (shortest wavelength) of the Lyman series ($n=\infty \to 1$).
options.C: It is the sum of the energies of all lines in the Lyman series.
options.D: It corresponds to the transition between Lyman and Balmer series.
